title: Producer-Consumer

validation.research: Five primary documentation sources: Eiffel’s Producer-consumer description; Microsoft BlockingCollection overview and producer-consumer dataflow documentation; official Python queue and threading documentation. Established roles, bounded-buffer form, synchronization, rate decoupling, blocking and completion are distinguished from implementation choices such as FIFO, local threads, immutable references, indexed reporting, and stop markers. Producer Consumer is a spelling alias; bounded-buffer problem is explained as the bounded form rather than a separate duplicate article or an alias implying every implementation is bounded. The reading-parser scenario, limits, code, outcome policy, and diagrams are original teaching material.

Instrumentation wraps real queue/thread/decode seams without replacing article coordination. No success guarantee for failed readings, deadline, unexpected-worker-death recovery, durable delivery, cancellation or CPU speedup is inferred.

example_limits: Original Python 3.11+ finite tuple-of-bytes batch; each immutable payload has at most eight bytes. Positive integer worker count/capacity and payload shape are validated before queue/thread creation. The coordinator is the sole producer; a bounded FIFO pending queue feeds fixed non-daemon consumers that decode ASCII digits into 0–100 units. Expected ValueError rejections become indexed error outcomes and do not kill workers. A separate unbounded outcome queue retains one result per finite input; final index sorting preserves report order without serializing processing. Input batch, active jobs, producer-held entry, and collected outcomes are outside the pending capacity limit. One private identity stop per consumer follows all jobs, every get balances task_done including stops/errors, then queue join and thread joins finish. Tests use real gated queue/thread/decode seams for capacity pressure and out-of-order completion, plus 360 records across one/two/four consumers. Assumes successful worker startup and finishing processing/outcome operations. No timeout, cancellation, unexpected-worker-death supervision, general resource-failure cleanup, durable delivery, exactly-once effects, fairness, processing-order, or CPU-parallel speedup guarantee. A continuous stream needs a concurrent result sink and bounds across all stages; a blocked sink can deadlock a coordinator waiting for completion.
